newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 4.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- CHANNEL TUNNEL CLEARED FOR PASSENGER SERVICES

Anglo-French safety authorities have given the green light for services to resume through the Channel tunnel following the fire two weeks ago. Eurostar, the passenger train service, will resume its services on Wednesday, but the vehicle shuttle services will not restart until next Tuesday.
-- LUCASVARITY TO CUT JOBS IN 250 MILLION STG SHAKE-UP

Anglo-US engineering group LucasVarity, which was formed by a merger earlier this year, has announced a large scale restructuring plan involving a number of disposals and job losses of up to 8,000 over the next year. Many of the redundancies are expected to fall at plants in the UK and continental Europe as the new company seeks to rationalise operations and withdraw from 13 non-core businesses.
-- SCOTTISH POWER TO SHED HALF SOUTHERN WORKFORCE

Unions representing workers at Southern Water have expressed dismay at news that the company's new owners, Scottish Power, are to cut 2000 jobs at the utility. Scottish acquired Southern Water earlier this year for 1.67 billion stg, and some job losses had been expected. But the scale of the cuts - almost half the workforce - and the fact that 700 come from the company's core water operations as opposed to via the sale of non-core companies, has surprised many employees.
-- NIELSEN PROMISES FAIR COMPETITION

US-based market research company ACNeilsen has bowed to pressure from the European Commission by pledging to end alleged anti-competitive practices in the European market. Nielsen had been accused of adopting unfair practices to impede the entry of its US rival Information Resources Inc into the European market for sales data from supermarkets. The role of the European Commission in bringing pressure to bear on Neilsen has been seen as a significant step towards improving co-operation in anti- trust activity between European and US agencies.
-- CARMAKERS FACE RULES ON RECYCLING

Proposals currently being drawn up by the European Commission would require all car manufacturers to take back disused cars and recycle their components. The environmental measures are likely to concern European vehicle manufacturers, many of whom have already concluded more flexible voluntary recycling agreements with a number of governments, mainly in northern Europe. The proposals are expected to be published next year and, if approved, would come into force from 2002.
-- P&O ATTACKS COUNCIL OVER 1 BILLION STG PROJECT

Birmingham City Council has come under attack on the first day of a public inquiry into plans to build a 1 billion stg semiconductor plant on a greenfield site on the outskirts of the city. Lawyers representing the property division of shipping company P&O accused the Council of abusing its planning powers by favouring its own land for the project ahead of P&O's adjacent site. An application by P&O to develop its site was rejected by the council in October, despite the plans for the micro- electronics plant on the neighboring site already having been approved.
-- RACAL HEADS BID FOR MOD SYSTEM

Racal Electronics, which on Monday issued an unexpected profits warning, has combined with rivals Siemens Plessey and ITT to offer a combined bid for the 2 billion stg MoD contract to replace the battlefield radio system of the British Army. The move marks a switch by the US firm ITT, which had previously been competing against a Racal-Siemens Plessey consortium. Racal, whose shares dropped sharply after Monday's profits warning, has also brought forward its interim results, announcing pre-tax profits of 21.3 million stg compared to 30.1 million stg last time.
-- CHEAPER MODEL HELPS PORSCHE TO SWIFT RECOVERY

Germany luxury sportscar manufacturer Porsche has reported a surge in turnover of 40 per cent in the first quarter, to Dm822m ($537 million). Sales were boosted by the marque's new Boxster, and by strong demand in the US for the classic 911. Sales of vehicles for the quarter to the end of October rose 55 per cent, to 6,181. Announcing the results, Porsche chief executive Wendelin Wiedeking said the group was 'on the right track', but analysts suggested that the company's forecasts for the full year are too modest.
-- BT AND MCI SEEK REGULATOR APPROVAL

British Telecom has set in motion the processes necessary for US approval of its proposed $20 billion merger with MCI. The two companies need to convince US telecoms regulator the Federal Communications Commission, the US Justice Department and the Committee on Foreign Investment in the US that the merger will not challenge either competition or fair trade, and that US telecoms customers in general and MCI's in particular will all benefit. The planned merger also had to pass European Union approval, although few difficulties are expected here.
-- CALLUNA SEEKS TO RAISE 5 MILLION STG

Calluna Technology, the Scotland-based technology company, is expected to unveil a 5 million stg rights issue on Wednesday as it seeks to raise funds to finance a big expansion of output. Calluna, which makes miniature disc drives, has made heavy losses since coming to the USM two years ago, and the issue is the company's second in six months. The funds raised will go towards production of Calluna's 520MB hard disc drives.
